problem:
Which of the following is a $3\times 1$ matrix?

$$
F=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 5 \\ 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,G=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,H=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following is a $3\times 2$ matrix?

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 7 \\ -2 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}],\,N=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \\ \sqrt{2} & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
- The matrix $L$ has $2$ rows and $2$ columns. So, its dimensions are $2\times 2.$ $\,\times $

- The matrix $M$ has $2$ rows and $3$ columns. So, its dimensions are $2\times 3.$ $\,\times $

- The matrix $N$ has $3$ rows and $2$ columns. So, its dimensions are $3\times 2.$ $\,✓$

Therefore, only $N$ is a $3\times 2$ matrix.
